subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 58-year-old man with prostate cancer undergoes external beam radiotherapy, which generates DNA double-strand breaks in tumor cells. Sequencing of the repaired junctions shows that broken ends were rejoined with small deletions of several nucleotides, and no homologous template was used.
question: Which of the following mechanisms best explains these findings?

options.text: Nonhomologous end joining, which joins DNA ends without requiring homology and may lose nucleotides
Homologous recombination, which uses a sister chromatid as a template
Mismatch repair, which corrects base mismatches introduced during replication
Nucleotide excision repair, which removes bulky helix-distorting lesions
Base excision repair, which removes altered bases through an AP site

explanation_correct: Nonhomologous end joining repairs double-strand breaks by bringing two DNA ends together without requiring a homologous template. Because the broken ends are processed before ligation, it is error-prone, so part of the DNA may be lost or translocated, which explains the small deletions at the junctions.

explanation_incorrect.B: Homologous recombination uses an intact homologous duplex as a template and restores the sequence accurately, so it would not leave these deletions.
explanation_incorrect.C: Mismatch repair acts on mismatched nucleotides in newly synthesized DNA, not on double-strand breaks.
explanation_incorrect.D: Nucleotide excision repair removes bulky adducts and pyrimidine dimers, not double-strand break junctions.
explanation_incorrect.E: Base excision repair removes individual altered bases and is unrelated to rejoining broken chromosome ends.

educationalObjective: Nonhomologous end joining repairs double-strand breaks without homology and is error-prone, often deleting nucleotides.
